terms.gloss: hire out one’s services, job by job
terms.grammar: verb phrase: operam meam locō; with ad and the accusative of the work, the ablative of the price
evidence: Plaut. Trin. 843–844: nam ego operam meam tribus nummīs hodiē locāvī ad artīs nūgātōriās
terms.comment: Latin has no word for a freelancer. What a freelancer does, hiring out his work for a price to whoever will pay, is what operam suam locāre says (Lewis & Short s.v. locō: to hire out one’s services); the freelancer himself is quī operam suam locat. We have found no term for it in Traupman, Morgan–Owens, or Levi–Bini.

phrases.latin: Huic ego diē nōmen Trinummō faciam: nam ego operam meam tribus nummīs hodiē locāvī ad artīs nūgātōriās.
phrases.english: I’ll call this day Threepenny Day: for today I’ve hired out my services for three pennies, for a piece of trickery.
I freelance for whoever I like.

phrases.latin: Quī operam suam locat, ipse sibi hōrās cōnstituit.
phrases.english: A freelancer sets his own hours.

sources: Lewis & Short: loco · Lewis & Short: opera
